steps.name: QC and PyDESeq2 differential expression
caveats: Deduplicate or aggregate any repeated gene symbols before building the matrix.
sample_01 shrinks size factors toward it for all samples; report its size factor explicitly rather than silently accepting it.
12 samples is the minimum this design supports: no covariate adjustment is possible beyond the condition term.
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control skin biopsies, after size-factor normalization that accounts for sample_01's ~4x-shallow library?
constraints: Python only (pandas, numpy, pydeseq2, matplotlib); no R
No imputation of sample_01: keep it in the primary fit and quantify its influence in the next step
Report the number of genes dropped by filtering and keep the full unfiltered results table on disk
steps.description: Load /eval-four-models-without-python-two-group-n6-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (first column gene symbol, 12000 genes x 12 sample columns) and merge on sample id with /eval-four-models-without-python-two-group-n6-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows; condition = treated or control). Quantify library sizes and confirm the shallow sample (sample_01, ~4x below median); plot pre-normalized library sizes and a PCA of log2(CPM+1) colored by condition to check whether sample_01 is also a global outlier or only shallow. Filter low-count genes (e.g. keep genes with >=10 counts in a minimal number of samples), fit PyDESeq2 with design '~condition' (treated vs control, 6v6 unpaired, single batch), run the Wald test with BH multiple-testing correction, and write the full results table (gene symbol, baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj) plus PCA, volcano and library-size figures. DESeq2 size factors are the correct handling of a shallow library: they rescale it rather than discard it.
acceptance_criteria: Library-size table written showing sample_01 at ~4x below median and every size factor reported
PCA labeled by condition produced; whether sample_01 clusters with its condition group is stated explicitly
DESeq2 size-factor-normalized DE table (all ~12000 genes) with log2FC, Wald stat, p-value, BH padj for treated vs control
Low-count filtering threshold documented (counts applied, genes retained reported)
volcano plot + top-gene MA/normalised-count plots written as PNG

steps.name: Sample_01 sensitivity analysis
caveats: With n=5 vs 6 the model has even less power; a gene significant only in the 12-sample fit is not necessarily false.
Correlate log2FC (shrunken) not raw p-values; p-values are unstable at this sample size.
steps.question: Does the shallow sample_01 drive or mask any treated-vs-control DE calls — do the significant genes survive its exclusion?
constraints: Keep the primary result (with sample_01) as the headline; the leave-one-out fit is a sensitivity analysis, not a replacement
If sample_01 is a within-condition PCA outlier of its own group, say so and report the leave-one-out result for that group direction explicitly
steps.description: Re-run the identical PyDESeq2 pipeline (same filtering, same design '~condition') on the 11 samples remaining after dropping sample_01, and compare against the full 12-sample fit: correlation of shrunken log2FC, overlap of significant genes (BH padj < 0.05 and |log2FC| >= 1), and a per-gene robustness label ('robust': significant and direction-consistent in both fits; 'sample_01-dependent': significant in only one fit). Also verify with the T1S1 PCA whether sample_01 sits apart from its condition group; if it does, report which condition it belongs to and whether its depth or its biology drives the difference. Output a sensitivity table and a short verdict on whether the shallow sample distorts the treated-vs-control answer.
acceptance_criteria: Side-by-side table: n DE genes (FDR<0.05) full-data vs sample_01-excluded, plus correlation of log2FC between the two fits
Every DE gene classified robust (passes FDR<0.05 and |log2FC| threshold in both fits) vs shallow-sample-sensitive (passes in only one)
Shrunken LFC (apeglm) used for ranking genes in both fits
A one-paragraph verdict stating whether the treated-vs-control signal is distorted by sample_01, and which genes the answer depends on

steps.name: Hallmark GSEA with sample_01 robustness check
caveats: With 12 samples, GSEA permutation is on gene sets not phenotypes (prerank); report FDR across the 50 sets, not per-gene p-values.
A shallow sample flattens its condition's ranking contribution in the full-data fit — that is exactly what the sensitivity run quantifies.
Blitzgsea (installed) is an acceptable substitute if gseapy.prerank misbehaves; do not reach for any network-backed enrichment service.
steps.question: Which MSigDB hallmark pathways are enriched in treated vs control skin, and which of those calls are robust to the shallow sample_01?
constraints: Python only; use gseapy.prerank (or blitzgsea) with the local GMT — no network, no enrichr/MSigDB download calls
Rank by the shrunken Wald statistic from the 12-sample fit; use gene symbols as-is (GMT is HGNC symbols)
Run the identical analysis on the 11-sample sensitivity ranking from T1S2 and report per-pathway robustness
steps.description: Rank all tested genes by the signed Wald statistic (or shrunken log2FC) from the 12-sample treated-vs-control PyDESeq2 fit and run GSEA pre-ranked (gseapy.prerank, weighted, nperm >= 1000) against the staged MSigDB human hallmark GMT (/mnt/refs/managed/msigdb-hallmark-human/2026.1/h.all.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt, 50 HALLMARK_* sets, HGNC symbols — matches the gene symbols in counts.csv). Repeat the identical prerank on the 11-sample (sample_01-excluded) ranking from T1S2 and report per-pathway NES, nominal p, and FDR q from both runs side by side, flagging hallmark calls that depend on the shallow sample. Write the full hallmark results table with leading-edge genes.
acceptance_criteria: Full ranked-list GSEA (nperm>=1000, gene set size 15-500) on all 50 HALLMARK_* sets with FDR q-values
Sensitivity GSEA on the sample_01-excluded ranking; per-pathway table showing which hallmark calls are robust to dropping sample_01
Leading-edge gene lists for the significant pathways written to disk

Bar/enrichment plot of significant hallmark pathways (both NES and FDR) as PNG; no gene set named a hallmark hit unless it clears FDR<0.25 (nominal p<0.05) in the full-data run and its robustness is annotated

plan.title: AD treated vs control DE and hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is a two-group contrast (6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch) on Salmon-derived gene-level integer counts (12000 genes x 12 samples, gene symbols in counts.csv). Genes are answered by a negative-binomial differential expression fit in PyDESeq2, whose median-of-ratios size factors are the statistically correct way to handle the one shallow library (sample_01 at ~4x below median) — not by discarding it. Because that sample is flagged by the profile and n is small, a leave-one-out sensitivity re-fit quantifies which DE genes depend on it. Hallmark pathways are answered by GSEA pre-ranked on the DE statistic against the staged MSigDB human hallmark GMT (50 sets, HGNC symbols, matching the gene-symbol identifier space of the counts), run twice — full-data and sample_01-excluded — so pathway calls inherit the same robustness check. All steps are Python (pandas/numpy/pydeseq2/gseapy); no R. Human hallmark GMT is confirmed present under /mnt/refs; pydeseq2 0.5.4 and gseapy 1.3.1 are installed.
